headline: Seven sectors carry more than 70 duty-side rows; six of them get 30 to 51 benefit-side rows — plastics converting gets 5
body:
Count every row in the register by what it does to a sector. Seven of the twenty sectors carry more than 70 duty-side rows: aluminium (165), waste (136), steel (127), batteries and solar (106), clean tech (97), power (75) and plastics converting (74). For six of the seven, the corpus also carries a substantial benefit side — between 30 benefit-side rows (waste) and 51 (aluminium).

Plastics converting carries 5. All five come from the Packaging and Packaging Waste Regulation itself — three transitional or mutual-recognition rights, one conformity simplification, one procedural right — and none of the register's other six files carries a single benefit-side row that names or reaches the sector. Three further PPWR rows are carry-overs whose level does not move; they are neutral and counted in neither column.

Across the seven files in the register, plastics converting is the addressee of [N] obligations and [N] prohibitions, the largest count of any sector below its parent. The register's incentive and support measures name it 5 times. The comparison is arithmetic: 74 burden-side measures against 5 benefit-side measures for the same slug, computed from the same rows that produce the sector's summary strip. Sectors with comparable burden counts carry between 30 (waste) and 51 (aluminium) rows on the benefit side. The register records what each act states; this finding records the difference between two of those counts.

evidence.notes: Counts are taken across every row of all seven register files, attributing a row to a sector where the slug appears in sectors_named or sectors_reached. Duty-side means valence Requirement or Prohibition plus benefit-side movements withdrawn (Support cut, Entitlement withdrawn); benefit-side means Simplification, Opportunity, Entitlement or Prohibition lifted; rows with direction 'unchanged' (Neutral) are excluded from both columns and reported separately (3 for chem/plastics). Sectors with more than 70 duty-side rows and their benefit-side counts: alu 165/51, waste 136/30, steel 127/48, batsol 106/47, clean 97/44, power 75/38, chem/plastics 74/5. The five cited rows are the complete benefit-side set for chem/plastics; a by-file split of the sector's rows puts all 74 duty-side and all 5 benefit-side rows in data/ppwr.json.

review.q: Draft pending George's edit. Two unresolved brackets: '[N] obligations and [N] prohibitions' — the finding body computes 74 duty-side rows in total but no obligation/prohibition split, so both brackets were left rather than filled. Also for George's check: 'name it 5 times' was filled from the body's 5 benefit-side rows, which are rights and simplifications attributed where the slug is named or reached — not strictly 'incentive and support measures [that] name it'.
